column11: The heaviest single check in the DevStg-Impl gate plan (docs/stack.ini "traceability" step; the BAR_RELEASE constant this Notes cell once named was retired with the bar axis at WI-498 slice 5): the full join/orphan/integrity/placeholder/schema pass over the whole spine (repo-review 2026-08-19 M-16). Measured 0.97s on this box (Windows 11, 24 cores, .venv Python 3.11.9; single-machine observation, not universal per the standing status.md rule -- re-measure locally before budgeting against it elsewhere). Budget carries ~5x headroom; Gate=warn because wall-clock is a noisy runtime metric (docs/stack.ini convention). No perf-metrics.json producer is wired yet (WI-481 seeds the registry only, per its own scope) -- this Notes figure is the manual measurement basis, not an automated baseline. fig: cmd=".venv/Scripts/python.exe project-trajectory/scripts/trace.py --root . --strict --no-placeholders --html --require-verified --strict-schema" rev=94489f7a

The dashboard-regeneration pair named in repo-review 2026-08-19 M-16, re-keyed at the WI-498 stage unification (derive_gate retired; derive_stage is the successor freshness recompute): derive_stage.py's fingerprint recompute feeds the PROJECT_STATE.html freshness recompute gen_trajectory.py performs next, which dominates the pair (the AST arch-map scan over all four spine registries). Both run in --check mode (compare-only, no write), matching the actual docs/stack.ini `derived-stage`/`trajectory-map` steps and the pre-commit hook's run-steps. Re-measured 6.82s median (6.79/6.82/6.93 over three warm runs) on this box (Windows 11, 24 cores, .venv Python 3.11.9; single-machine, not universal) -- within noise of the pre-unification 6.46s. Budget carries ~3x headroom; Gate=warn (noisy runtime metric). No perf-metrics.json producer is wired (WI-481 scope: registry rows + basis only). fig: cmd=".venv/Scripts/python.exe project-trajectory/scripts/derive_stage.py --root . --check && .venv/Scripts/python.exe project-trajectory/scripts/gen_trajectory.py --root . --check" rev=73663c3d

column11: The full commit-time floor every session pays, end to end: the batched freshness/integrity run-steps (okf, trajectory-map, status-map, open-items, trajectory, registry-integrity, derived-stage, skills-sync, skills-index, prompt-catalog, approval-fresh, staged-divergence), check_trajectory.py --staged, the privacy/secrets scans and the format check (repo-review 2026-08-19 M-16's motivating case: 'nothing would notice' a regression here). RE-KEYED AND RE-MEASURED at the WI-498 close (the PB-002 precedent, applied to the row four lines below it that the same sweep missed): the step list said `derived-gate`, a step deleted with docs/gate, so the row attributed its figure to a floor the hook no longer runs -- the successor step is `derived-stage`. Re-measured 9.00s median (8.99/9.00/9.11 over three warm runs) on this box (Windows 11, 24 cores, .venv Python 3.11.9; single-machine, not universal) -- up from the pre-unification 7.7s, still dominated by the trajectory-map step's gen_trajectory.py --check cost (PB-002). Budget carries ~3x headroom; Gate=warn (noisy runtime metric). No perf-metrics.json producer is wired (WI-481 scope: registry rows + basis only). Measured through the INSTALLED hook (.githooks/pre-commit, the copy git actually runs here): the shipped project-trajectory/hooks/pre-commit resolves scripts/ against an adopting repo's layout and cannot be timed standalone in the meta-repo. fig: cmd="sh .githooks/pre-commit" rev=8885a30a
